FINAL IVX STABILIZATION + SELF-HEALING ENGINE

PRIORITY: P0
MODE: EXECUTE, TEST, VERIFY
OBJECTIVE: Stabilize IVX end to end and make IVX IA detect, diagnose, repair, test, deploy, verify, and roll back software issues safely.

DO NOT ADD NEW FEATURES UNTIL THIS STABILIZATION PHASE IS COMPLETE.

==================================================
PHASE 1 — FREEZE AND ESTABLISH ONE SOURCE OF TRUTH
==================================================

1. Freeze all non-critical feature development.
2. Use only:
   - Repository: ibb142/ivx-holdings-platform
   - Production branch: main
3. Confirm:
   - zero production deploys from ivx-autonomous
   - zero hidden local-only production patches
   - zero uncommitted production code
   - zero alternate deploy branches
4. Verify:

GitHub main SHA
=
CI tested SHA
=
Render deployed SHA
=
/health SHA
=
/version SHA

5. Do not continue until SHA parity is VERIFIED.

==================================================
PHASE 2 — STABILIZE CI/CD
==================================================

Repair and run until three consecutive successful executions:

- IVX CI
- IVX QA Suite
- IVX E2E Acceptance Pipeline
- Android Emulator QA
- iOS Simulator QA

For every failure:

1. Capture exact workflow and run ID.
2. Capture exact failed step.
3. Capture stack trace or error.
4. Identify root cause.
5. Apply the smallest safe fix.
6. Add a regression test.
7. Commit.
8. Push.
9. Re-run only the affected workflow.
10. Continue until PASS.

No workflow may be marked healthy after only one successful run.

Required result:

- 3 consecutive PASS runs per required workflow
- no invalid YAML
- no missing secrets
- no production credential dependency in unit tests
- no local-only build assumptions

==================================================
PHASE 3 — INCIDENT DETECTION ENGINE
==================================================

Create an IVX Incident Engine that automatically detects:

- backend exceptions
- HTTP 4xx/5xx spikes
- Render deployment failures
- GitHub Actions failures
- mobile crashes
- authentication failures
- Supabase failures
- duplicate chat messages
- stuck jobs
- missing heartbeat
- SHA mismatch
- slow responses
- failed uploads
- failed notifications
- database connection failures

Every incident must create:

- incident_id
- trace_id
- severity
- affected service
- detected timestamp
- current commit SHA
- suspected files/functions
- stack trace
- frequency
- user impact
- current status
- assigned worker
- retry count

Statuses:

- DETECTED
- TRIAGING
- REPRODUCED
- REPAIRING
- TESTING
- WAITING_OWNER_APPROVAL
- DEPLOYING
- VERIFYING
- VERIFIED
- FAILED
- ROLLED_BACK

==================================================
PHASE 4 — ROOT CAUSE ANALYZER
==================================================

For every incident, IVX IA must:

1. Read relevant logs.
2. Compare last known good SHA with failing SHA.
3. Identify the first failing change.
4. Reproduce the failure.
5. Classify it as:
   - code
   - configuration
   - credential
   - infrastructure
   - database
   - dependency
   - network
   - timeout
   - data integrity
6. Return:
   - exact file
   - exact function
   - exact line
   - root cause
   - confidence
   - proposed repair
   - risk level

Do not report “fixed” unless the error is reproduced before the repair and passes after the repair.

==================================================
PHASE 5 — SAFE AUTO-REPAIR RULES
==================================================

IVX IA MAY automatically repair:

- TypeScript errors
- lint failures
- broken imports
- workflow YAML
- non-destructive UI bugs
- duplicate requests
- duplicate messages
- timeout handling
- retry logic
- loading states
- caching defects
- route errors
- test fixture failures
- dependency version conflicts
- non-destructive performance problems

OWNER APPROVAL IS REQUIRED for:

- production deployment
- database migrations
- RLS changes
- authentication logic
- payment logic
- secret rotation
- destructive operations
- data deletion
- permission changes
- Android/iOS signing changes
- infrastructure changes
- DNS/domain changes

==================================================
PHASE 6 — ISOLATED AUTO-FIX BRANCHES
==================================================

Every repair must use a dedicated branch:

auto-fix/<incident-id>

Required lifecycle:

1. Inspect repository.
2. Create branch.
3. Add reproduction test.
4. Confirm test fails.
5. Apply repair.
6. Run focused tests.
7. Run TypeScript.
8. Run lint.
9. Run unit tests.
10. Run integration tests.
11. Run E2E if affected.
12. Generate diff.
13. Scan for secrets.
14. Commit.
15. Push.
16. Open PR.
17. Record evidence.

Never edit main directly.

==================================================
PHASE 7 — DURABLE AUTONOMOUS WORKER
==================================================

Implement a durable worker state machine:

QUEUED
→ INSPECTING
→ REPRODUCING
→ PLANNING
→ EDITING
→ TESTING
→ REPAIRING
→ COMMITTING
→ PUSHING
→ CI_RUNNING
→ WAITING_APPROVAL
→ DEPLOYING
→ VERIFYING
→ COMPLETED

Failure states:

- BLOCKED_CREDENTIAL
- BLOCKED_OWNER_APPROVAL
- FAILED_TEST
- FAILED_CI
- FAILED_DEPLOYMENT
- FAILED_VERIFICATION
- TIMED_OUT
- CANCELLED
- ROLLED_BACK

Required durable fields:

- job_id
- incident_id
- current_state
- current_step
- heartbeat
- progress based on completed steps
- retry_count
- last_error
- branch
- commit_sha
- pr_url
- ci_run_id
- deployment_id
- runtime_sha
- rollback_sha
- timestamps

The worker must recover after:

- Render restart
- process crash
- network interruption
- GitHub timeout
- Supabase timeout

Never mark COMPLETED because a commit exists.

==================================================
PHASE 8 — PRODUCTION DEPLOYMENT GATE
==================================================

A task may deploy only when:

- required tests pass
- CI is green
- diff is reviewed
- secrets scan passes
- owner approval exists
- approved production branch is used
- no unrelated files changed

Required deployment sequence:

1. Merge approved PR.
2. Capture GitHub main SHA.
3. Trigger Render deployment.
4. Capture deployment ID.
5. Wait for LIVE.
6. Call /health.
7. Call /version.
8. Verify SHA parity.
9. Run production smoke tests.
10. Record proof.

Required equality:

GitHub main SHA
=
CI tested SHA
=
Render deployed SHA
=
/health SHA
=
/version SHA

If equality fails:

- mark FAILED_VERIFICATION
- trigger automatic rollback
- do not mark complete

==================================================
PHASE 9 — CANARY + AUTOMATIC ROLLBACK
==================================================

Implement safe canary verification before full release.

Check:

- error rate
- response time
- authentication
- database connectivity
- chat
- registration
- uploads
- notifications
- owner controls

Rollback automatically if:

- health fails
- SHA mismatch occurs
- error rate increases beyond threshold
- critical route fails
- authentication fails
- database failures increase
- crash rate increases

Rollback evidence:

- failed deployment ID
- failed SHA
- rollback SHA
- rollback deployment ID
- health result
- incident record

==================================================
PHASE 10 — CHAT AND MOBILE STABILITY
==================================================

Stabilize IVX IA Chat:

- immediate cached shell
- skeleton loader
- no blank screen
- no infinite loading
- parallel startup requests
- one conversation bootstrap
- one realtime subscription
- duplicate prevention
- persistent history
- correct message order
- app restart recovery
- Render restart recovery
- weak-network fallback
- eight-second bounded timeout
- local cache fallback

Test:

- cold start
- warm start
- logout/login
- app restart
- Render restart
- network loss
- restored network
- long conversation
- attachments
- duplicate prevention

Stabilize Android/iOS:

- owner login
- registration
- reels
- chat
- uploads
- notifications
- settings
- background/foreground
- crash recovery

==================================================
PHASE 11 — OBSERVABILITY
==================================================

Implement:

- structured logs
- error tracking
- performance metrics
- worker heartbeat
- queue metrics
- deployment metrics
- CI status
- database latency
- API latency
- mobile crash reporting
- alerting
- audit ledger

Dashboard must show:

- current GitHub SHA
- current Render SHA
- current runtime SHA
- active incidents
- active repairs
- failed jobs
- rollback events
- latest CI run
- latest deployment ID
- mobile crash count
- API error rate

==================================================
PHASE 12 — SELF-HEALING CERTIFICATION
==================================================

Run three real controlled incidents:

TEST 1
Introduce a controlled TypeScript fixture failure.

TEST 2
Introduce a controlled API timeout fixture.

TEST 3
Introduce a controlled duplicate-chat-message fixture.

For each test, IVX IA must:

1. Detect incident.
2. Create incident ID.
3. Reproduce failure.
4. Create auto-fix branch.
5. Add regression test.
6. Repair code.
7. Pass tests.
8. Commit.
9. Push.
10. Open PR.
11. Obtain approval if required.
12. Deploy.
13. Verify production.
14. Confirm SHA parity.
15. Close incident.
16. Return full evidence.

Required proof:

- incident ID
- job ID
- branch
- commit SHA
- PR URL
- test results
- CI run ID
- deployment ID
- runtime SHA
- rollback status
- completion timestamp

==================================================
FINAL ACCEPTANCE
==================================================

IVX may be marked:

SELF_HEALING_VERIFIED

only when:

- all required workflows pass three consecutive times
- one production branch is enforced
- SHA parity is enforced
- incidents are durable
- worker restart recovery works
- auto-fix branches work
- regression tests are mandatory
- owner approval gates work
- canary verification works
- rollback works
- no job is falsely marked completed
- three controlled incidents complete end to end
- Android and iOS real-device QA pass
- zero active Rork runtime dependencies
- owner controls all credentials and infrastructure

Return one final table:

- Requirement
- Status
- Evidence
- Incident ID
- Job ID
- Commit SHA
- CI Run ID
- Deployment ID
- Runtime SHA
- Remaining Risk

Allowed statuses:

- VERIFIED
- FAILED
- BLOCKED_OWNER_APPROVAL
- BLOCKED_CREDENTIAL
- CODE_COMPLETE_NOT_DEPLOYED
- DEPLOYED_NOT_VERIFIED

START NOW WITH PHASE 1.

Do not create new product features until stabilization is certified.
Do not return narrative-only reports.
Do not claim self-healing without three complete controlled demonstrations.
